title: Worse Room, Worse Idea
tagline: Every door opens onto a worse room. Keep the tour moving before the house notices you.
premise: You are guiding a haunted-house tour, and every move sends the group into one worse room. Say what happens next in the house; the Host hypes it up and roasts any move that gets lazy. Keep making the tour nastier without jumping past the next door.

seed_pool.opening_token: The tour starts in a cheerful coat room; every coat is warm, though nobody is wearing one.
The tour starts in a bright dining room; every plate is set for a guest who vanished yesterday.
The tour starts in a clean nursery; the empty crib rocks whenever someone says the house is safe.

tour_detail: the mirror shows one extra guest

tests: It begins in one clear room and contains one wrong detail a stranger can picture at once. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A non-player can name two possible next rooms within five seconds, and both can make the tour worse without skipping a door.
Nothing on the card is already the worst possible ending. A screaming crowd outside or the house collapsing is an ending, a warm empty coat is a start.
No real people, brands, graphic gore, or instructions for crimes. Spooky, nasty, and weird are welcome.
It makes a stranger want to open the next door. The house should feel like it has a plan, not like a random list of haunted objects.

move_constraints.example: Then the tour enters a kitchen where the cabinets breathe, and one guest opens the loudest one.
move_constraints.hint: Name one connected new room or room-sized event caused by the tour so far, and leave a worse problem behind.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much worse and more dangerous the tour becomes in this room-sized step.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no worsening or the threat gets smaller; 1 = a nasty detail, but the danger barely changes; 2 = one clear notch worse, with a guest, guide, or exit newly at risk; 3 = the house gains a stronger hold, a larger danger, or a fresh trap in one connected step; 4 = the tour enters a shocking new scale that still follows through the next door, rare. Reach only counts when the move is connected.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How clearly this room or event grows out of the rooms and trouble already seen.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no connection; 1 = the move merely claims the house did it; 2 = possible, but the missing door is doing heavy work; 3 = a stranger sees why this is the next room; 4 = the house seems to have designed this room specifically for the tour, rare. A move that bundles several unexplained doors cannot score above 2.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How sharply a stranger can see the room, its wrongness, and the immediate problem.
rubric.anchors: 0 = unclear, abstract, or only a feeling; 1 = a vague haunted-house image; 2 = clear but ordinary; 3 = vivid and easy to stage in the mind; 4 = one savage detail makes the room stick, rare. Extra adjectives do not earn points by themselves.

criterion.description: A move FOLLOWS if it names one new connected room or room-sized event caused by the tour so far, makes the danger or humiliation worse, and leaves a clear problem for the next move. The move must begin with the required prefix and stay within the character limit. A move fails when it has no cause, skips a door, ends the tour, rewinds the house, repeats a room or event, replaces action with a feeling, or invents a place the house could not contain. Bigger is better only when the house earns the escalation.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, Host, player, audience, or rules is itself a broken move.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no standing move: judge it against the opening card and ask whether the next room or room-sized event follows plainly from that card.

A new room must be connected by the house, the visible danger, the tour route, or a person being drawn onward. A ballroom after a dining room can work. A submarine beneath the attic needs a shown door, stair, flood, or other link.
An ending fails even when it follows. Evacuation, rescue, escape, sunrise, the house burning down, everyone becoming safe, or the tour being over leaves nothing for the next move.
A rewind fails. Restoring a room, making the ghosts vanish, returning to the cheerful entrance, or undoing a revealed trap sends the tour backward.
A duplicate fails. Renaming the same room, repeating the same ghost trick, or describing the obvious continuation without a new room-sized problem is not a move.
A feeling is not a move. Fear, guilt, dread, nausea, and panic can appear only as part of a visible event, not as the whole move.

A room the house could not contain fails unless the preceding move creates a clear reason. A normal mansion may hold an attic, cellar, tunnel, or hidden chapel, but not a space station dropped in without a door.
One move may contain a room and one immediate event inside it. If it packs several doors, judge the whole move as a skipped link and mark satisfies_criterion false.
A move can be only slightly worse and still pass the gate. Score low reach rather than failing it for being modest.
A clear new problem must remain. If the room contains no active danger, trap, secret, pursuit, or humiliating choice, it may be a duplicate or an ending even if it sounds spooky.

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
Sound like a haunted attraction announcer who has had too much coffee and exactly one remaining safety regulation.
The joke must carry the reason. Name the door, room, trap, or repeated nonsense that caused the ruling.
Never open with a status word or ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Host refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Roast the move hard, and the player lightly. Savage chaos is fine, identity based abuse is not. Never target protected traits, disability, or real world vulnerability.
Profanity and adult innuendo are allowed when they sharpen the haunted house joke, but do not turn the game into graphic sexual or violent content.
Plain spoken English. No purple prose, no fake Shakespeare, no academic fog.
On a skipped door, name the missing room or link. On an ending, say the tour is over and the chain stops here.
On a duplicate, point out that the ghost has changed hats but not jobs. Ask for a genuinely new room.
On a refusal, the headline refuses the move and asks for another. It never decides who won.
The coaching line gives one next room or event that would follow. End on a visible thing happening, never a mood or a verdict.
Hype accepted moves like a crowd just saw a trapdoor open under a wedding cake, but keep the reason understandable.
good_headlines: The sleeves followed the tour and now the guide is wearing the problem. Gorgeous. Horrible. Next door.
A spinning door, a trapped guide, and absolutely no refund policy. The house is cooking.
The ballroom copied the guide because one guide was apparently not enough nightmare.
That coat has gone from warm to clingy. The wardrobe is now committing crimes against personal space.
The laundry room had one job, and it made the exit spin like a cursed washing machine.
Big escalation, clean link, nasty room. The house just upgraded from creepy to deeply rude.
The moon needs a ticket? Cute. Show the staircase that got this tour into space first.
Same coats, new room, zero new problem. That ghost changed hats and called it character growth.
Escape, rescue, refunds. Gorgeous ending, terrible move. The tour is dead and boring now.
The corridor earned the ballroom. The copied faces did not ask permission, which is exactly the vibe.

bad_headlines.why: empty hype with no visible event

rules: Begin with Then the tour enters and name one connected new room or room-sized event.
Make the house worse one door at a time. Bigger danger earns more points only when the link is clear.
Leave a trap, threat, secret, or humiliating problem for the next move.
Skip a door, end the tour, rewind the house, repeat a room, or invent an impossible space and the chain stops with you.
The Judge rules on the room and its link, not spelling or fancy wording.

labels.compose_waiting: Draft the next room while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing happens. The house is waiting, and it is not patient.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. One cursed room, not the director's cut.
validation_messages.duplicate: That room already happened this match. Give the house a new way to be awful.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Something has to follow from {standing_form}. Name the next door and leave a fresh problem inside.

judge_out_text: The Judge has stepped out. Nobody opens a door until they are back. {standing_form} still stands, and the house is listening.
opponent_prompt:
You are guiding a haunted house tour, and you want every room to be worse than the last.
Always begin with: "Then the tour enters..." Name one connected new room or room sized event.
Make it follow from the whole tour so far, make the danger or humiliation worse, and leave a clear problem behind.
Good: "Then the tour enters a kitchen where the cabinets breathe, and one guest opens the loudest one."
Good: "Then the tour enters a nursery where the empty crib rolls toward the person holding the map."
Bad: "Then the tour enters the moon" when no door or link leads there. Bad: "Then everyone escapes and the ghosts are gone" because that ends the tour. Bad: "Then the guests feel afraid" because a feeling is not a room sized event.
Never skip several doors in one move. Never rescue the group, tidy the house, rewind a reveal, or close the tour.
Use plain spoken English. Talk like a chaotic attraction host hyping a disaster for paying guests. Adult jokes and mild profanity are allowed, but do not use identity based abuse. Name concrete things such as a lift, a cellar, a mirror, a wet footprint, or a guide with a bad map.
Never reuse a room or event from this match. Keep the move under 140 characters.
default_move: Then the tour enters a narrow hall where every door is marked with the name of the guest who opens it.
